newsitem.title: UK: Metals end LME upbeat, lifted by shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Metals end LME upbeat, lifted by shortcovering.

text.p: Base metal prices largely skipped higher during Friday afternoon LME trading, boosted by end-week covering ahead of Monday's pricing against the July "third Wednesday", traders said.
Copper attempted to erode overhead resistance, zinc neared recent highs, aluminium built on underlying support, while other metals also gained.
"It was not too busy this morning, but there short-covering this afternoon," one trader said.
Copper was defended on an initial dip to $2,250, and largely ignored the 2,800-tonne stock increase, focussing instead on July date borrowing ahead of Monday.
Spread activity was volatile, but by the close of the kerb cash/threes was at a backwardation of some $135. Earlier, July/one day traded at $13.
Three months prices talled in mid-$2,290s, but still ended $16 higher at $2,284.

Zinc was also massaged by spread activity, with traders citing the possibility of a squeeze around the September date. High backwardations in September pulled the cash/threes contango in to $4/7, against levels above $10 on Thursday.

Forward prices got within $4 of testing last week's 6-3/4 year highs of $1,495 before settling back at $1,486, up $7. The objective is $1,500, although there is likely to be producer selling there, traders said.
Aluminium paid little lasting attention to a 6,900-tonne stock increase, whch was believed to reflect off-warrant consignment metal being registered.
Again, recent good support helped the market limit the downside, and last trade was at $1,582, up $12.
Nickel prices came to life during the afternoon rings and kerb, with the market clearing the $6,900 level to end $115 firmer at $6,965.
Traders said the market was helped by the general trend, although initial steadiness was due to a 438-tonne stock decline.
Lead progressed higher as well, albeit slowly, helped by its sister metal zinc, and by the end of the kerb was standing $7 higher at $667. The market's target is still $675.
Tin business was largely subdued, before a late mark-up on the kerb. Three months concluded at $5,550, up $30.
Alloy was neglected for most of the session, closing at a stable $1,420/30 a tonne.
